titulo: Práctica extra de Inglés — Luz Sees the Light: vocabulario en oraciones, la historia página por página y cómo se lee una novela gráfica

temas.nombre: Luz Sees the Light · Vocabulary in sentences
temas.explicacion:
Habilidad del temario: To use vocabulary words in sentences (ecology, conservation, sanctuary, recycle, frequent, sufficient, oasis, permission, installing, abandoned).

Definiciones literales del libro (Luz Sees the Light):
  • frequent — If something is frequent, it happens often.
  • sufficient — If something is sufficient, it is just what is needed and no more.
  • oasis — An oasis is a relaxing or peaceful spot in an area that is unpleasant in some way.
  • permission — If you get permission, someone who is in charge allows you to do what you asked to do.
  • installing — If you are installing something, you are setting it up so it is ready to use.
  • abandoned — If a place is abandoned, it is no longer cared for or used.
Palabras del temario sin definición en las fotos del libro (significado general del diccionario):
  • ecology — the study of how living things relate to each other and to their environment.
  • conservation — protecting nature and natural resources and using them carefully so they are not wasted.
  • sanctuary — a safe place where people, animals or plants are protected.
  • recycle — to treat used things (paper, glass, plastic, metal) so they can be used again.
Cómo aparecen en el cuento:
  • “Luz and her friends enjoy listening to music and frequent trips to the mall.”
  • “…they need to prepare for more blackouts by becoming more self-sufficient.” (self-sufficient = able to take care of your own needs)
  • “I’m going to turn you into an oasis in the city—a neighborhood food park!”
  • “But I think I need to apply for permission from the city first…”
  • “Installing park benches.”
  • “I’ve got a surprise… remember that old abandoned lot at the corner?”
temas.microleccion:
Ejemplo con OTRA palabra (no es del temario): crowded = full of people.
Paso 1 — Leo la definición: «full of people».
Paso 2 — Busco en la oración una pista que encaje: «The bus was so ______ that I had to stand.» → si tuve que ir de pie, el bus estaba lleno de gente.
Paso 3 — Pongo la palabra y releo: «The bus was so crowded that I had to stand.» ✔️
Paso 4 — Para ESCRIBIR mi propia oración: sujeto + verbo + la palabra + una pista que muestre el significado: «The market is crowded on Saturdays because everyone buys food.»

temas.nombre: Luz Sees the Light · Comprehension: Luz’s idea and her problems
temas.explicacion:
Habilidad del temario: To answer comprehension questions.

Lo que pasa en la primera parte (textos literales de los globos del libro):
  1. Power outage: “Hmm. No TV, no cooking, no air conditioning… What’s going on?” “Is it another power outage?” “Oh! Everyone’s just hanging out in the yard!”
  2. “I could go shopping, but it’s not like I can buy those sneakers… I don’t think I even want them anymore!” “I know! It’s time to start working on my secret community project!”
  3. A speeding car: “YIKES!” “Hey! I was trying to enjoy a peaceful moment!” “It would be nice to get a break from speeding cars on this street!”
  4. “Get ready, you old patch of gravel and garbage. I’m going to turn you into an oasis in the city—a neighborhood food park! Full of beautiful life!”
  5. “We need soil and plants and benches and maybe a playground.” “And hey, what about a place for a band to play, or we could use that wall for outdoor movies.” “I just need to get lots of neighbors on board.” “So I gotta make posters and flyers.” “But I think I need to apply for permission from the city first and—” “Whew, this is already exhausting!!”
  6. Luz tells Robert: “…and we can grow our own food so we don’t need to get it from other countries!” Robert: “Grow food? What’s wrong with buying groceries?” Luz: “Well, almost all our food is shipped from far away, so when oil gets too expensive for transportation, or it runs out entirely, it won’t matter because we’ll have a neighborhood farm!”
  7. Anika: “Ha! That’s nuts! You know, there are supermarkets, Luz.” “A farm in the city! A tractor wouldn’t even fit on this lot!” Luz: “It’s crazy, right?”
  8. Luz alone: “Maybe I can’t turn a garbage dump into a garden. Everyone will say a farm park is a stupid idea.” “But don’t people see that things are changing? And that we need to change, too?”
  9. LATER THAT WEEK… Luz eats snacks on the couch, turns off the TV and says “Well, here goes nothing.” A neighbor: “I don’t want to buy whatever it is you’re selling!” Others: “Nope!” “Not interested!” Luz: “Oh, what’s the point?”
  10. The mail arrives: “Maybe there’s an answer from the city about getting permission to use the lot!” — “Argh! Just junk mail.” “All right. That’s it. If no one’s going to help me, I’ll turn that lot into a food park myself!”
  11. A FEW MINUTES LATER… “Okay, I got gloves and a garbage bag.” “Time to take out the trash!” She finds rats: “Oh, GROSS!” “Ack! This is all too hard!” “I’m sorry… I tried!”
  12. She thinks: “Here I am, trying to get my neighbors together, and no one’s around—or even interested! I try to get my friends on board, and they laugh at me!” “I can’t do it by myself.” “And why should I? The park is for everyone, not just for me!”
temas.microleccion:
Ejemplo con OTRA historia (no es del libro): «Tomás quiere pintar un mural en la pared gris de la escuela. Le pregunta a tres compañeros y todos le dicen “No tengo tiempo”. Tomás compra pintura con sus ahorros, pero la pared es enorme. Se sienta y piensa: “Solo no puedo. Además, el mural es de todos.”»
Pregunta: Why does Tomás stop painting alone?
Paso 1 — Busco la evidencia: lo que dice o piensa el personaje → «Solo no puedo» y «el mural es de todos».
Paso 2 — Respondo con oración completa usando la evidencia: He stops because the wall is too big for one person, and he thinks the mural is for everyone, so everyone should help.
Paso 3 — En una novela gráfica la evidencia está en los globos, en los recuadros y también en los dibujos (caras, lo que pasa en el fondo).

temas.nombre: Luz Sees the Light · Comprehension: teamwork and Friendship Park
temas.explicacion:
Habilidad del temario: To answer comprehension questions.

Lo que pasa en la segunda parte (textos literales del libro):
  1. Robert and Anika arrive. Anika: “So, like, Robert told me about what your park idea was all about, and well… it sounds like A LOT of work—” Luz: “Okay, I get it! You think it’s a stupid idea!” Both: “NO, WE WANT TO HELP!!” Anika: “I think having a park in our neighborhood is a great idea.” Robert: “And you know I love vegetables!” Luz: “Thank you!” “What are friends for?”
  2. Robert: “How about we make posters for the neighborhood?” Anika: “I’ll leave that to the design expert. Catch you guys later!” Luz: “Do you think we could design them on your computer?” “We could print out a bunch of copies and then— hand them out to friends and neighbors— and put them in mailboxes, and on streetlamps and notice boards…”
  3. Captions: “THE GANG DISCUSSES THEIR ACTION PLAN FOR THE NEXT TWO WEEKS.” “FOOTWORK AND POSTERS SPREAD THE NEWS.” “TAKING CARE OF (STINKY) BUSINESS!” “LAYING DOWN GRASS” “PLANTING TREES” “INSTALLING PARK BENCHES” “OLD TIRES BECOME NEW PLANTER BOXES.” “BUILDING A CONCERT AREA… …AND A PLAYGROUND” “GORD’S IDEA GETS APPROVED BY THE CITY.” (Car-Free Sundays) “MR. AND MRS. DESOUZA SHARE THEIR PLANTS.” “Yay, we’re all done!!!”
  4. Sunday: “Not another blackout.” “Ah, who cares! We’ve got a party to go to.” “And it doesn’t need any electricity!” On the street: “There are no cars on the street!” “Yeah, that was Gord’s idea! He got the city to do this new thing where our street is blocked off so people can walk anywhere!”
  5. “Well, now it’s a park!!” Luz: “This place was a patch of concrete with no sign of life, right where our neighborhood could have a place for people to hang out and play and…” “No, this is for the earth!” “It was a lot of work, but everyone did a part!”
  6. Luz: “Well, this park is proof that we’re not alone, and we can all work together and help each other to learn stuff and grow stuff and make stuff and build stuff…” “…So that in the end, whatever happens, we can rely on ourselves for the things we really need! No more imports or giant malls!”
  7. Robert gives Luz a package: “I made these to say thanks for, you know, being my friend since I’m new to the city.” Anika: “These are your own designs! Talk about limited edition—this is the only pair of its kind!” Gord: “Heh, nice to see friends together in Friendship Park. How appropriate!”
temas.microleccion:
Ejemplo con OTRA historia (no es del libro): «Sofía quiere una biblioteca en el aula. Mateo dice: “¡Yo traigo una repisa!” Valentina dice: “Yo hago los carteles.” La maestra trae libros viejos de su casa. Al final, Sofía dice: “Fue mucho trabajo, pero cada uno puso su parte.”»
Pregunta: Who did what?
Paso 1 — Hago una tabla: Mateo → la repisa · Valentina → los carteles · la maestra → los libros.
Paso 2 — Pregunta de inferencia: What is the lesson? → la pista está en lo que dice Sofía al final: When everyone does a part, a big project becomes possible.
Paso 3 — En la novela gráfica, los recuadros (captions) te dicen quién hizo cada cosa: «MR. AND MRS. DESOUZA SHARE THEIR PLANTS.»

temas.nombre: Luz Sees the Light · How to read a graphic novel
temas.explicacion:
Habilidad del temario: To identify the distinguishing characteristics of a graphic novel.

Characteristics of a graphic novel (con ejemplos de Luz Sees the Light):
  • Panels: the boxes with pictures. You read them in order: left to right, top to bottom. Some panels are big (the whole page with “Well, now it’s a park!!”) and some are small circles (like Luz’s face saying “I’ve got a surprise…”).
  • Speech bubbles: what characters SAY. “Hey! I was trying to enjoy a peaceful moment!”
  • Thought bubbles: cloud shapes with little circles; what characters THINK. “Here I am, trying to get my neighbors together, and no one’s around—or even interested!”
  • Shouting: big, bold letters or a spiky bubble. “NO, WE WANT TO HELP!!”
  • Captions: boxes that tell time, place or what is happening. “LATER THAT WEEK…”, “BUT WITHIN MOMENTS…”, “A FEW MINUTES LATER…”, “THE GANG DISCUSSES THEIR ACTION PLAN FOR THE NEXT TWO WEEKS.”
  • Sound words (onomatopoeia): krunch krunch, clik, Flump!, CHRRRK!, SNATCH!, BZZT!!, YAWN!, TWEET TWEET!
  • Drawings show feelings and movement: drops of sweat (nervous or tired), lines around the head (surprise), motion lines (moving fast), a red background (anger), hearts (love and thanks).
  • Time passing: repeating a picture (the clock SUN 11:57 → SUN 11:59) or many small panels with captions (two weeks of work on one page).
  • Like every story: characters, setting, problem and solution.
temas.microleccion:
Ejemplo con OTRA historieta (no es del libro): una página tiene 4 paneles.
Panel 1 (arriba a la izquierda): un recuadro dice «MONDAY MORNING…» → es un caption (dice cuándo).
Panel 2 (arriba a la derecha): un perro salta y aparece «WOOF!» → sound word.
Panel 3 (abajo a la izquierda): la niña tiene gotitas alrededor de la cabeza → el dibujo muestra que está nerviosa.
Panel 4 (abajo a la derecha): un globo con picos dice «STOP!!» en letras gruesas → está gritando.
Orden de lectura: 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 (izquierda a derecha, de arriba hacia abajo), igual que un texto.
